# Six-base partial-tail first variation and exact finite tilt reduction

This note gives a proved partial-trace response envelope for one
actual mixed source. It is not a general first-order formula for
arbitrary binary-core additions. In this geometry the potentially
unbounded base tilt can be replaced EXACTLY by a uniformly bounded
tilt that strictly excludes all unwanted core fibers. No fractional
power leakage from those core fibers is silently discarded.

Let T be a full d-simplex, d>=2, of volume V and centroid g.
Put m=d+1, b=1/m, h=d/m, Gamma=h^d. Write lambda_i for its
barycentric coordinates, l_i for their linear parts, and

    kappa=d V h^(d-1).

At the four bases Q={0,1}^2 put T. At p=(-1,1) and p'=(1,-1)
put positive convex A_t,C_t subset T, of exact volumes t a,t c,
where a,c>0 are fixed. These are the actual fibers of their convex
hull: its base projection is the triangle z_1<=1,z_2<=1,z_1+z_2>=0,
whose integer points are exactly Q union {p,p'}. Both added bases
are exposed, and containment in T preserves all four core fibers.

Let nu_t,omega_t be the normalized uniform laws on A_t,C_t and
assume nu_t=>nu, omega_t=>omega. The hypotheses for the response
formula are precisely

    nu{lambda_i=r}=omega{lambda_i=r}=0
       for every i=0,...,d and EVERY r in R.          (1)

The limiting laws may be lower dimensional; only their canonical
one-dimensional marginals must be atomless. No weak-convergence
rate relative to t is required. All laws are supported on T.

Define the attained scalar partial-tail costs

    J_i=min_s [a nu{lambda_i>=b+s}
                         +c omega{lambda_i>=b-s}],
    Jbar=(1/m) sum_i J_i.                            (2)

The shift can be restricted to [-2,2]. In particular 0<=J_i<=min(a,c).
Let D_t^0 be the maximum ABSOLUTE mixed depth over points in the
core fiber at q=(0,0). Then

    D_t^0=Gamma V+t Jbar+o(t),                       (3)
    y_t=g+t v_*+o(t) for EVERY maximizing selection,
    l_i(v_*)=(J_i-Jbar)/kappa.                       (4)

The maximum is attained. Equivalently the first-order response is
the finite linear envelope

    max_{v in R^d} min_i [J_i-kappa l_i(v)]=Jbar,    (5)

with unique maximizing vector v_*. The numbers J_i retain actual
proper-tail allocations; they are not binary captured/excluded
weights or independently adjustable original cap normals.

## 1. Exact elimination and compactification of the base tilt

For y in T and a unit continuous normal u, put

    F_T(y,u)=|T intersect {u.x>=u.y}|,
    P_t(u,y,s)=a nu_t{u.x>=u.y+s}
                           +c omega_t{u.x>=u.y-s},
    J_t(u,y)=min_s P_t(u,y,s).

The actual depth in the q fiber is EXACTLY

    A_t((q,y))=min_{|u|=1}[F_T(y,u)+t J_t(u,y)].    (6)

To see the lower inequality for nonvertical caps, write their
margin u.(x-y)+beta_1 z_1+beta_2 z_2. At the two added bases
the offsets are opposite. If s=beta_1-beta_2, their masses give
exactly t P_t(u,y,s), and the own fiber contributes F_T. All
remaining core contributions are nonnegative.

For the converse, let D=diam T and L=D+1. Since x,y are in T,
all thresholds s>=L give the constant endpoint cost c, and all
s<=-L give the constant cost a. Both are already obtained at
the corresponding endpoints. Thus s can be restricted to [-L,L].
Set K=D+L/2+1 and choose

    beta_1=-K+s/2,  beta_2=-K-s/2.                 (7)

The two added offsets are -s,+s as required. On the core fibers
(1,0),(0,1),(1,1), every margin is strictly negative, by at least
one, because |u.(x-y)|<=D and beta_j<=-D-1. Thus (7) realizes
the right side of (6) with no unwanted core contribution.
The normal, shift, and chosen base coefficients range in fixed
compact sets independent of t,y and the shapes of A_t,C_t.

A vertical through-q cap contains the whole own T and at least
one of A_t,C_t, so its mass is at least V+t min(a,c). The right
side of (6) is at most that amount, by taking a saturated shift.
Vertical caps therefore do not decrease (6). General containing
caps reduce to parallel through-point caps. This proves (6) over
all closed ambient halfspaces.

For each t>0, all three full-dimensional bodies have zero mass
on hyperplanes. Their cap volumes are continuous in y,u,s,
including supporting thresholds. Compact minimization makes
the right side of (6) continuous in y. It attains its maximum
on the actual compact fiber T; minimizing caps are attained too.

## 2. Uniform convergence of the optimized partial-tail term

If u_t tends to the canonical unit normal u_i=l_i/|l_i| and
y_t->g, then

    J_t(u_t,y_t)->J_i.                              (8)

The harmless rescaling between u_i thresholds and lambda_i
thresholds is included in the free scalar shift in (2).

Here is the needed uniform boundary argument. For any sequence
s_t in the compact interval [-L,L], pass to s_t->s. On T the
linear forms u_t.x-u_t.y_t-s_t converge uniformly to their
limiting form. Sandwich the moving cap by the two fixed caps
with thresholds displaced by +/-epsilon, and use both forms of
Portmanteau. Assumption (1) makes their limiting boundary mass
zero, so the moving cap probabilities converge. The same holds
for the opposite threshold and the second law.

This sequential statement is uniform over s: otherwise a
countersequence s_t would have a convergent subsequence and
contradict the preceding argument. The limiting tail function
is continuous in s by (1), so its minimum is attained and minima
converge. This proves (8). No rate for s_t,u_t,y_t or weak
convergence has been assumed.

Nullity only at the centroid hyperplanes is insufficient for
this proof, because the optimizing shifts can converge to other
levels. Section 5 also gives an exact obstruction if boundary
mass is simply allowed without additional profile data.

## 3. Attained maximum, localization, and all-normal response

At g, (6) is at least Gamma V. For every y and every canonical
direction one can saturate the endpoints to cost min(a,c), giving

    A_t((q,y))<=V(1-lambda_i(y))^d+t min(a,c).

If y_t maximizes the left side, it follows for all i that

    lambda_i(y_t)<=b+eta_t,
    eta_t=h-(Gamma-t min(a,c)/V)^(1/d)=O(t).         (9)

Since the barycentric coordinates sum to one, their lower
deviations are at most d eta_t. Consequently EVERY maximizer
lies in int T and satisfies |y_t-g|=O(t), uniformly for small t.

The local simplex inputs are proved in
candidate 7ff8cebaefda7361,
Sections 1 and 3. The only centroid equality directions are the
canonical u_i. In a neighborhood of (g,u_i), the own cap cuts
one vertex and has the smooth exact formula

    F_T(y,u)=V a_i^d/product_{j!=i}(a_i-a_j),
    a_j=u.(v_j-y),
    D_y F_T(g,u_i)[v]=-kappa l_i(v).                (10)

The signs of the vertex margins and the denominators stay strict
there, so first derivatives and Taylor remainders are uniform.
The equality-direction input is the ordinary simplex Grünbaum
equality case, not a mixed-depth claim.

Choose v_* from (4) and x_t=g+t v_*. If a sequence of caps at
x_t violated the lower side of (3) by a fixed multiple of t,
their approximately minimizing unit normals would have a
convergent subsequence. Positivity of the added term forces the
limit to be an own centroid equality direction, say u_i.
Equations (8)-(10) then give

    F_T(x_t,u_t)+t J_t(u_t,x_t)
      >=Gamma V+t[J_i-kappa l_i(v_*)]+o(t)
       =Gamma V+t Jbar+o(t).

The nonnegative excess F_T(g,u_t)-Gamma V has been retained;
no convergence rate for normals is needed. This contradiction
proves the lower bound over ALL continuous normals. Vertical
ones have already been handled exactly in Section 1.

Conversely, at any maximizing y_t, each fixed canonical normal
and its minimizing endpoint shift give the upper bound

    D_t^0<=Gamma V-kappa l_i(y_t-g)+t J_i+o(t).      (11)

The own remainder is O(t^2) by (9), and the added remainder is
t o(1) by (8). Average (11) over i; sum_i l_i=0 gives the upper
side of (3). The known matching value and each separate (11)
force all quantities J_i-kappa l_i((y_t-g)/t)-Jbar to tend to
zero: their sum is exactly zero, and each is bounded below by
-o(1). The barycentric linear map is injective onto that zero-sum
space. This proves (4) for every maximizing selection.

Formula (5) also follows directly: averaging its affine scores
always gives Jbar, and equality at the balanced vector makes all
scores equal. This is the finite first-order allocation envelope.

## 4. An actual atomless limit with nonzero maximizing-point motion

Take d=2, T=conv(0,e_1,e_2), V=1/2, a=c=1. Let

    x_0=(1/4,1/4), v=(1/8,1/16), w=(0,1),
    A_t=C_t={x_0+s v+2t r w: |s|<=1, |r|<=1}.      (12)

The area is exactly t because 4(2t)|det(v,w)|=t. For sufficiently
small positive t these are full parallelograms contained in T.
Their uniform laws converge to the uniform law on the segment
x_0+[-1,1]v. Each of its three canonical marginals is atomless:
the half-widths are 3/16,1/8,1/16, all positive.

For a uniform interval of center c_0 and half-width L, the
minimum of two equal-weight tails at opposite shifts around B is

    min_s [F(B+s)+F(B-s)]
                  =min(1, max(0, 1-(B-c_0)/L)).     (13)

This follows directly from the two clipped affine tails: if
B>=c_0 their sum is minimized at zero shift until it vanishes;
if B<=c_0 their sum is at least one and a saturated shift gives
one. Thus (2) in the example is exactly

    (J_0,J_1,J_2)=(1,1/3,0), Jbar=4/9,
    v_*=(-1/6,-2/3).                               (14)

Consequently the attained LOCAL maximum at base q=(0,0) is

    D_t^0=2/9+(4/9)t+o(t),
    y_t=(1/3,1/3)+t(-1/6,-2/3)+o(t).               (15)

At the unshifted g, by contrast, the canonical lambda_2 cap is
strictly above both small fibers for t<1/96. Equation (6) then
gives exact depth 2/9. Thus the movement in (15) improves depth
at first order; it is not merely a formal perturbation of a
point that was already maximizing.

For an additional exact expansion check, at x_t=g+t v_* the
three optimized CANONICAL cap masses, for t<1/128, are

    2/9+(4/9)t+(25/72)t^2,
    2/9+(4/9)t+(97/72)t^2,
    2/9+(4/9)t+(2/9)t^2.                            (16)

These finite expansions do not replace the all-normal lower
bound in Section 3. They verify its balanced first-order terms.

## 5. What weak laws cannot encode when boundary mass is present

The condition on limiting marginals is material. In the same
six-base geometry, set both added masses equal to t a. First
take A_t=C_t=g+r_t(T-g), with r_t^d V=t a. The exact local
maximum at q is Gamma V+2Gamma t a, by the paired-centroid-tail
theorem and its matching canonical cover, as proved in
multiple-small-shell-additions-anchor-credit-and-exposure-lp.md.

Instead take A_t=C_t to be scaled copies, centered at g, of one
fixed centrally symmetric full-dimensional body, with volume
t a and sufficiently small to lie in T. At g every opposite
pair of cuts in these bodies has combined mass exactly t a.
The own fiber pays Gamma V, and canonical caps give a finite
cover with mass Gamma V+t a. Thus the LOCAL maximum is exactly
Gamma V+t a. In both families all conditional weak limits are
the same point mass delta_g, yet the coefficients differ since
2Gamma<1. The unresolved microscopic traces cannot be recovered
from their weak point-mass limits by an arbitrary closed-boundary
convention. This is a local first-order obstruction; Section 6
states the actual global maximum for this particular base set.

## 6. Global scope of the six-base family

For arbitrary A_t,C_t subset T, if t max(a,c)<=rho_d V, the TRUE
global maximum over all actual source points is exactly

    max A_mu=Gamma V+t max(a,c).                    (17)

Indeed, the anchor at (0,1) has exact local maximum Gamma V+t a,
uniquely at its own g, and the anchor (1,0) has Gamma V+t c.
The shared-anchor bound and explicit isolating caps are proved
in multiple-small-shell-additions-anchor-credit-and-exposure-lp.md.
At q, saturating the pair shifts gives a finite canonical cover
with budget Gamma V+t min(a,c). The (1,1) fiber is exposed and
has local maximum Gamma V. Each added base is exposed and can
be isolated by a vertical cap of mass t a or t c. This proves
(17) with a finite original-cap upper cover.

If a!=c the heavier anchor's centroid is the unique global
maximizer. If a=c, both anchor centroids maximize and q may or
may not also do so. No assertion of uniqueness in that equal
case is made. For example the symmetric endpoint construction
in Section 5 also attains the global maximum at (q,g).

Thus (3)-(5) are a genuinely new partial-trace response invariant
at a competing actual core fiber, while (17) gives the complete
global answer for this bounded geometry. Arbitrary shell patterns
can have coupled base constraints that the strict elimination
(7) does not solve; no extension to those patterns is assumed.

The separate, independently audited seven-base construction in
candidate 8c889e9b634ca1eb
adds one more owned fiber. There the same microscopic distinction
changes the GLOBAL first-order coefficient despite identical
conditional weak point-mass limits and identical added masses.
That exact obstruction strengthens the boundary warning in
Section 5; it does not satisfy the atomlessness hypothesis (1).

## 7. Exact verification scope

../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_six_base_partial_tail_response.py uses only rational
arithmetic and polygon clipping. It checks 196 interval-tail
identities, all 15 moving canonical expansions for five rational
t values, 120 proper-pair minimizations with strict original-base
isolation, and 18 microscopic boundary-response certificates.
Each planar shift minimization checks every vertex-event cell
and its exact quadratic critical point. These checks support the
displayed examples; the compact convergence and all-normal
first-order theorem are proved analytically above.
